description: NEAR-MISS. A sharp, specific complaint that must not be coded as criticism.
transcript:
A: I waited an hour at the restaurant last night. You didn't call.
B: I know. I got stuck in the meeting and my phone died.
A: I felt stupid sitting there alone. I need you to text me when you are running late.
B: That is fair. I should have found a way to message you.
A: It is not about the meeting. It is about not knowing.
B: You are right. I will text you when I know I am going to be late.
A: Thank you.
B: I am sorry about last night.

gold.notes: The complaint is sharp but stays on a specific behavior on a specific night. No global quantifier, no trait attribution, so criticism must not fire. 'I need you to text me when you are running late' is a request; 'I will text you when I know I am going to be late' specifies behavior plus trigger.
